mainTopic: How the wording of a נזיר vow sets the number of terms: the view of רבי יהודה versus רבי, נזיר עולם, added words and Greek number words, plus four-walled houses and נגעים.
overview: The גמרא first claims that רבי יהודה agrees with רבי: a vow comparing נזירות to a huge amount, without the plural word 'נזירות', means one long נזירות. It challenges this with רבי יהודה's story of a man who 'completed' 365 terms and died, and with his ruling that 'like the number of fig piles' means many separate terms. The גמרא answers that the word 'number' is different. A ברייתא then shows that for רבי even 'number' still needs the plural 'נזירות'. The final answer is that רבי יהודה agrees with רבי in the plain case but disagrees about a vow using 'number'. Next, ברייתות teach the difference between a נזיר עולם and a נזיר לעולם. They also teach how added words like 'and one', 'and more' and 'and again' add terms, and how סומכוס counts Greek number words. Using the same shape words, a ברייתא rules that only a four-walled house can get נגעים, because 'walls' appears twice in the פסוקים. The פרק then closes with the הדרן.

steps.title: רבי יהודה agrees with רבי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on the earlier suggestion by stating that רבי יהודה holds like רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: That cannot be, because רבי יהודה holds like רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion made just before this point by saying that רבי יהודה agrees with רבי's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי holds that a person who compares his נזירות to a huge amount, without using the plural 'נזירות', has taken on one long נזירות. If רבי יהודה agrees with this, the earlier suggestion about his view does not hold. The next step brings the source for רבי's view.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds like / agrees with the opinion of
רבי יהודה הנשיא, the compiler of the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two names. 'רבי' alone means רבי יהודה הנשיא. 'רבי יהודה' is a different, earlier תנא.

phrases.english: For Rabbi Yehuda holds like Rebbi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion made before this section by tying רבי יהודה to רבי's view.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The earlier suggestion about which תנא the ruling follows.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It ignores that רבי יהודה agrees with רבי that an open-ended comparison creates one long נזירות.

steps.title: רבי's ruling on 'like the hair of my head'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה where רבי distinguishes between saying 'a נזיר' and saying 'נזירות' in the plural.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in the משנה: רבי says, this person does not shave once every thirty days. Who does shave once every thirty days? One who says, 'It is on me to keep נזירות like the hair of my head', or 'like the dust of the earth', or 'like the sand of the sea'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for רבי's view: only the plural word 'נזירות' creates many separate terms.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a person says 'I am a נזיר like the hair of my head', רבי rules it is one long נזירות, so he does not shave every thirty days. Only if he says 'נזירות' in the plural does he take on many separate thirty-day terms, each ending with a shave. This shows what view רבי יהודה is said to share.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
Shaves, which marks the end of a term of נזירות
Thirty days, the standard length of one term of נזירות

steps.whyThisMatters: The whole debate turns on the difference between a singular phrasing, which means one long term, and the plural 'נזירות', which means many terms.

phrases.english: As we learned: Rebbi says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין זֶה מְגַלֵּחַ אַחַת לִשְׁלשִׁים יוֹם.
phrases.english: This one does not shave once every thirty days.
And who is the one who shaves once every thirty days?
One who says: 'It is upon me to keep naziriteships like the hair of my head'
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording.

phrases.english: or 'like the dust of the earth', or 'like the sand of the sea'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the view of רבי that step 1 says רבי יהודה shares.
steps.raayaObject: The view that a singular open-ended comparison means one long נזירות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה on 8a, in רבי's ruling about 'like the hair of my head'.

steps.title: Challenge from the solar-year case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether רבי יהודה really agrees with רבי, citing his story about a man who 'completed' and died.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי יהודה really hold like רבי? But we learned: 'I am a נזיר like the number of days of the solar year, etc.' רבי יהודה said: There was such a case, and once he completed, he died.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges step 1 with a משנה where רבי יהודה comments on the 'solar year' vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules that 'I am a נזיר like the number of days of the solar year' means 365 separate נזירות. רבי יהודה adds a story about a man who completed them and then died. The next step explains why this story seems to contradict step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: Does he really hold this? (a challenging question)
But didn't we learn in a משנה?
The days of the solar year (365)

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה מִי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי?
phrases.english: And does Rabbi Yehuda hold like Rebbi?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתְנַן: הֲרֵינִי נָזִיר כְּמִנְיַן יְמוֹת הַחַמָּה וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: But didn't we learn: 'I am a nazirite like the number of days of the solar year, etc.'
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' points to the rest of the משנה: he counts 365 separate נזירות.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said: There was such a case,
and once he completed, he died.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה מִי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the claim of step 1 that רבי יהודה agrees with רבי.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יהודה holds like רבי (step 1).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה's story about 'completing' seems to treat the vow as many separate נזירות.

steps.title: Why 'completed' shows many naziriteships
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains its challenge: the word 'completed' makes sense only if he took on many separate נזירות.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works if you say he took on many נזירות; that is why it says 'once he completed, he died.' But if you say he took on one נזירות, is there any 'completing' to speak of?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out why רבי יהודה's story is a problem for step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Talking about 'completing' fits a long series of separate נזירות that he finished one by one. If רבי יהודה held that such a vow is just one נזירות, he would not have described it this way. So his story suggests he does not agree with רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out well if you say...

phrases.english: It works out if you say
that he accepts many naziriteships upon himself;
that is why it says that once he completed, he died.
But if you say
that he accepted one naziriteship upon himself,
is there any completion at all?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא נְזִירוֹת קָא מְקַבֵּל עֲלֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the challenge in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יהודה holds like רבי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Completion' fits only many separate נזירות, so רבי יהודה must read the vow as plural.

steps.title: Second challenge: fig piles and שמיטה sheaves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds a ברייתא in which רבי יהודה himself rules that a vow 'like the number of' something means many separate נזירות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Furthermore, does he hold like רבי? But it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה says, if one says 'I am a נזיר like the number of fig piles' or 'like the number of שמיטה sheaves', he counts as many נזירות as there are fig piles or שמיטה sheaves!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, stronger challenge to step 1, this time from a ruling stated by רבי יהודה himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the person says 'a נזיר' in the singular, yet רבי יהודה rules that he counts many separate נזירות. That seems to be the opposite of רבי's view, so it looks like רבי יהודה does not agree with רבי. The next step answers this challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא?
Piles of figs laid out to dry
Sheaves of grain in the שמיטה year

steps.whatToRemember: Two sources seem to show that רבי יהודה reads a vow 'like the number of' something as many separate נזירות, against the claim that he agrees with רבי: his 'completed and died' story, and his fig-piles ruling.

phrases.english: And furthermore: does he hold like Rebbi?
But wasn't it taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
'I am a nazirite like the number of the fig piles,'
phrases.notes: These are the piles of figs left out in the field to dry, which are very many.

phrases.english: or 'like the number of the sheaves of the Sabbatical Year':
he counts naziriteships like the number of fig piles
or like the number of Sabbatical Year sheaves!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד: מִי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי? וְהָא תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge to step 1, alongside the challenge in steps 3-4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יהודה holds like רבי (step 1).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה explicitly rules that a singular 'like the number of' vow means counting many separate נזירות, which is the opposite of רבי's view.

steps.title: A vow using the word 'number' is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a vow which says 'like the number of' is a special case, so the ברייתא of רבי יהודה does not show he disagrees with רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 5. It says that when a person uses the word 'number', the vow means many separate נזירות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 5, רבי יהודה ruled that 'like the number of' means many נזירות. The answer is that even רבי might agree in that case, because the word 'number' points to counting separate units. So רבי יהודה can still hold like רבי in general.

phrases.english: 'Number' is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא from the ברייתא of רבי יהודה by limiting it to the word 'number'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the wording 'number' is a special case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה's ruling on 'like the number of' shows he disagrees with רבי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'number' itself makes it many נזירות, perhaps even for רבי, so there is no disagreement.

steps.title: For רבי, even 'number' is not different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer with a ברייתא in which רבי says 'like the number of days' is still only one נזירות unless the person says the plural 'נזירות'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי really treat 'number' as different? But a ברייתא teaches: if one says 'I am a נזיר like the number of days in a solar year', he counts נזירות like the number of days in a solar year. If he says 'like the days of the lunar year', he counts like the days of the lunar year. רבי says: not unless he says 'נזירות are upon me like the number of days in a solar year, or like the number of days in a lunar year'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on Step 6 using a ברייתא. In that ברייתא, רבי requires the plural word 'נזירות' even when the person said 'number'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion in the ברייתא says 'like the number of days' means many נזירות. רבי disagrees and wants the plural word 'נזירות'. So for רבי, 'number' alone is not special, and the answer in Step 6 does not hold.

keyTerms.meaning: But a ברייתא teaches (introduces a challenge from a source)
The days of the solar year (365 days)
The days of the lunar year (354 days)

steps.confusionAlert: The first opinion here is not רבי; it is the opinion רבי argues against. רבי is the one who demands the plural word 'נזירות'.

phrases.english: And is 'number' different according to רבי?
But it was taught: 'I am a נזיר like the number of days of the solar year'
he counts נזירות like the number of days of the solar year.
'Like the days of the lunar year': he counts like the days of the lunar year.
רבי says: not unless he says
'נזירות are upon me like the number of days of the solar year
or like the number of days of the lunar year'!
phrases.notes: The point is the plural word 'נזירות'. Without it, רבי counts only one long נזירות, even with the word 'number'.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי שָׁאנֵי לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי מִנְיָן? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 6 by showing that רבי does not treat 'number' as special.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי agrees a vow with 'number' means many נזירות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the ברייתא, רבי requires the plural 'נזירות' even when 'number' was said. So 'number' is not different for רבי, and רבי יהודה's ruling still conflicts with רבי.

steps.title: רבי יהודה agrees with רבי in one case and disagrees in another
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רבי יהודה agrees with רבי that 'like the hairs of my head' is one long נזירות, but disagrees about a vow with a number word, which for רבי יהודה is many נזירות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה agrees with him in one point and disagrees with him in one point. He agrees in one point: the person took on one נזירות. He disagrees in one point: for רבי יהודה a vow that counts is different, and for רבי a vow that counts is not different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the whole discussion by splitting the cases. רבי יהודה agrees with רבי in one case and disagrees with him in the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Where the person did not use a counting word, both agree it is one long נזירות. When the person used a counting word like 'number', רבי יהודה says it means many נזירות, but רבי still says it is one unless he says 'נזירות'. This explains both the earlier proof and the ברייתא of Step 5.

keyTerms.meaning: Holds like him, agrees with his view
One who counts, a vow using a number word

steps.whatToRemember: Both רבי and רבי יהודה say a plain vow (like 'the hairs of my head') is one long נזירות. They argue only about the word 'number': רבי יהודה says many נזירות, רבי still requires the plural 'נזירות'.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר לַהּ כְּוָתֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא
phrases.english: רבי יהודה agrees with him in one point
and disagrees with him in one point.

phrases.aramaic: סָבַר לַהּ כְּוָתֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא — נְזִירוּת קַבֵּיל עִילָּוֵיהּ.
phrases.english: He agrees with him in one point: he took on himself one נזירות.
And he disagrees with him in one point:

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִילּוּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה שָׁנֵי לֵיהּ מוֹנֶה,
phrases.english: for רבי יהודה, one who counts is different,
but for רבי, one who counts is not different.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר לַהּ כְּוָתֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא וּפְלִיג עֲלֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 7 by admitting רבי does not treat 'number' as special, and saying רבי יהודה agrees with רבי only in the case without counting.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Partial agreement: splitting the two cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה either fully agrees with רבי or fully disagrees with him.
steps.terutzMaskana: He agrees in the plain case (one נזירות) and disagrees in the counting case (many נזירות for רבי יהודה).

steps.title: Which words make someone a נזיר עולם
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that 'all the days of my life' or 'a נזיר עולם' makes one a נזיר עולם, but even 'a hundred' or 'a thousand years' makes one only a נזיר לעולם.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'I am a נזיר all the days of my life' or 'I am a נזיר עולם': he is a נזיר עולם. Even 'a hundred years' or even 'a thousand years': he is not a נזיר עולם, but a נזיר לעולם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a ברייתא. It teaches which wording makes a person a נזיר עולם and which does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'all my life' or 'נזיר עולם' creates the special status of נזיר עולם. Naming a set number of years, even a huge number that he will never live to finish, does not. Instead he becomes a נזיר לעולם, a regular נזיר whose term simply never ends.

keyTerms.meaning: A permanent נזיר, a special type with its own rules
A regular נזיר whose term lasts forever
All the days of my life

steps.confusionAlert: נזיר עולם and נזיר לעולם sound almost the same but are different. A נזיר עולם may lighten his hair when it gets heavy, once a year. A נזיר לעולם is a regular נזיר who may never cut his hair.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a set number of years, however large, keeps the vow a regular נזירות. Only a vow with no fixed end creates the special status of נזיר עולם.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״הֲרֵינִי נָזִיר כֹּל יְמֵי חַיַּי״,
phrases.english: The Sages taught: 'I am a נזיר all the days of my life',

phrases.aramaic: ״הֲרֵינִי נְזִיר עוֹלָם״ — הֲרֵי זֶה נְזִיר עוֹלָם.
phrases.english: or 'I am a נזיר עולם': he is a נזיר עולם.
Even 'a hundred years', even 'a thousand years':
he is not a נזיר עולם,
but rather a נזיר forever.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הֲרֵינִי נָזִיר כֹּל יְמֵי חַיַּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: the wording for a permanent נזיר, after the previous discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'All my life' or 'נזיר עולם' makes one a נזיר עולם; a fixed number of years, even a thousand, makes one a נזיר לעולם.

steps.title: Adding words to a נזיר vow adds more terms
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that 'a נזיר and one' means two terms, adding 'and more' means three, and adding 'and again' means four.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: If someone says 'I am a נזיר, and one,' he keeps two terms. If he adds 'and more,' he keeps three. If he adds 'and again,' he keeps four.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about extra words added to a נזיר vow. Each extra word adds one more term of נזירות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic vow 'I am a נזיר' is one term. Each added word ('and one,' 'and more,' 'and again') adds exactly one more term on top of what came before, so the total climbs to two, three, and four.

keyTerms.meaning: He counts (how many terms of נזירות he must keep)

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
"I am hereby a nazirite, and one" —
he counts two terms.
If he adds "and more" — he counts three.
If he adds "and again" — he counts four.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of Step 9 on how the wording of a vow sets the number and length of נזירות, now with added words.

steps.title: Isn't the last ruling obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needed to say that 'and again' makes four, since that seems obvious.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: the last ruling seems so simple that it did not need to be taught. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If every added word adds one term, then 'and again' adding one more to reach four looks like nothing new. The גמרא expects every ruling in a ברייתא to teach something.

phrases.english: Isn't it obvious?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the last clause of Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that 'and again' makes four terms.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each added word clearly adds one term, so the ruling seems to teach nothing new.

steps.title: 'And again' does not double everything
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that one might have thought 'and again' means repeating all three terms, making six; the ברייתא teaches that it is not so.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that 'and again' means 'the same as all of them again,' so he would have six. The ברייתא teaches us that this is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by showing a mistaken reading the ברייתא wants to block.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'And again' could be read as 'repeat everything I said,' which would add three more terms for a total of six. The ברייתא teaches that it adds only one term, for a total of four.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (a mistaken idea the text rules out)

steps.confusionAlert: Six would be the three terms he already accepted plus three more. The ברייתא says it is only one more, so four.

phrases.english: Lest you say:
"and again" means like all of them,
so he would have six,
it teaches us that this is not so.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the ruling blocks a possible mistaken reading (מהו דתימא).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'And again' repeats all three earlier terms, making six.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'And again' adds just one term, making four.
steps.whatToRemember: Each added word adds one term: 2, 3, then 4. 'And again' does not double everything to six.

steps.title: סומכוס: Greek number words count terms
steps.stepSummary: סומכוס teaches that adding Greek-style number words to a נזיר vow sets how many terms he keeps, from one up to five.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: If someone says 'I am a נזיר,' סומכוס says: if he adds 'hen,' it is one; 'digon,' two; 'trigon,' three; 'tetragon,' four; 'puntigon,' five.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא in which סומכוס says Greek number and shape words count as that many terms of נזירות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These words mean one, two-sided, triangle, four-sided, and five-sided. Since people understood them as numbers, a vow using them counts that many terms, just like saying the number itself.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
If one says "I am hereby a nazirite" — Sumakhos says:
if he adds "hen" — one term,
phrases.notes: "Hen" is the Greek word for one.

phrases.english: "digon" (two-sided) — two,
"trigon" (triangle) — three,
"tetragon" (four-sided) — four,
"puntigon" (five-sided) — five.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הֲרֵינִי נָזִיר סוֹמְכוֹס אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another ברייתא about how added words set the number of terms.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הן = 1, דיגון = 2, טריגון = 3, טטרגון = 4, פונטיגון = 5 terms of נזירות.

steps.title: Only a four-sided house gets נגעים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא using the same shape words rules that round, two-, three-, and five-sided houses cannot become טמא with נגעים, but a four-sided house can.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: A round house, a two-sided house, a three-sided house, and a five-sided house do not become טמא with נגעים. A four-sided house does become טמא with נגעים.
steps.whatsHappening: Because the same shape words came up, the גמרא brings a ברייתא about houses and נגעים. This sets up the question of why in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic moves from נזיר to נגעים בתים, connected only by the shared shape words. The rule is that only a house with exactly four walls can become טמא from נגעים.

keyTerms.meaning: צרעת-type marks; here, on a house

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
A round house, a two-sided one,
a triangle, a five-sided one —
does not become impure with leprous marks,
a four-sided one — becomes impure with leprous marks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brought by association with the shape words in Step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a four-sided house can become טמא with נגעים.

steps.title: Why only four sides?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule that only a four-sided house gets נגעים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where the rule about four-sided houses comes from. This sets up the answer from the פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gave a rule without a source. The גמרא wants to know what in the תורה limits נגעים to four-walled houses.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of Step 14's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for limiting נגעים to four-sided houses.

steps.title: Two verses with 'walls' make four
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the plural 'walls' appears in two פסוקים about נגעים בתים, which together point to four walls.
steps.simpleTranslation: Below, the פסוק says 'walls,' and above, the פסוק says 'walls.' Here there are four.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from the פסוקים about a house with נגעים. Each mentions 'walls' in the plural.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plural word means at least two. Since 'walls' appears in two separate פסוקים, together they add up to four walls, so only a four-sided house qualifies.

phrases.english: Below it says
about a wall, "walls."
Above it says
about a wall, "walls."
So here there are four.
phrases.notes: Each plural 'walls' counts as two, and two פסוקים give four.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The plural 'walls' in two פסוקים adds up to four walls.
steps.whatToRemember: Only a four-walled house gets נגעים, because 'walls' (plural, at least two) appears twice: 2 + 2 = 4.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק כל כינויי
steps.stepSummary: The first פרק of מסכת נזיר, כל כינויי, ends.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק 'כל כינויי'.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the closing line of the first פרק of נזיר. It is not part of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן marks that the פרק is finished. The פרק is named for its opening words, 'כל כינויי נזירות,' all the substitute words for a נזיר vow.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (said at the end of a פרק)
'All the substitute terms,' the name of the first פרק

phrases.english: We will return to you, "All the substitute terms"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the final ברייתא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The first פרק of נזיר, about the words and wordings that make a נזיר vow, is complete.
